findings.defect: The advertised consequence is vacuous. Since u_{v,a} <= 1 on Q(G), nu(P) <= 1 <= |C|, so the recursion Phi(P') <= |C| Phi(P)/nu(P) has right-hand side >= Phi(P) for every polytope and never certifies any decrease; 'the first quantitative bound on what one cut buys' buys nothing. Only the one-cut inequality max_{P'} u_{v,ibar} <= q(x)/M(v,i) has content, and that is a two-line consequence of dropping nonnegative terms.

verdict: NEW-THEOREM, but a small one, and smaller than the route presents it. DID THE OBJECT CHANGE? Only mildly: kappa(G) is the resolvent of lem:survival-contract's reduced survival operator S over C, i.e. the paper's own survival-time quantity (prop:escape-family's display sum_k S^k 1 <= kappa(x)/(1-lambda)) restricted from V to C; the restriction is not a collapse and the route PROVES the separation from the escape class through prop:hz, which is to its credit. But the restricted object was already named by round 13 and its main property recorded as (v11), so the paper's inventory is the wrong yardstick for calling it new. CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? Not circular: no oracle, no target-equivalent hypothesis, and {kappa <= poly} does have a member outside the eight bounds on the reachable subgame (HZ(n), prop:hz). But it is close to vacuous in reach: that member is one the paper already solves by hand with the same algorithm, and the paper's own (v11) reading -- 'any algorithm conditional on kappa is worthless' -- is now proved rather than overturned. RUBRIC: at least one proved result of class new-relation exists (ht:lem-sigmin, which I re-verified on 250 freshly generated members of R, and ht:cor-rlambda), so new-theorem stands; two of six results are restatements (ht:prop-cutform, ht:prop-tworounds) and must not be integrated as results. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it: not 'is R a polynomial class' (rem:lcp already records the prior art that answers it for all of R), and not 'find a family in R with lambda_min superpolynomially small' (a non sequitur, refuted by the route's own W_10) -- it is: exhibit a stopping SSG family, in R or out of it, on which the tangent cut M7 together with the three readings of rem:own-successor over the Z-seeded transport polytope is silent at a value-distinguishing vertex for superpolynomially many rounds UNDER EVERY TIE-BREAK among the lexicographic optima, since every silence recorded so far (BC(2,s) in the paper, W_10 here) is a one- or two-round artefact of a particular tie-break. WOULD INTEGRATING MAKE THE PAPER BETTER? Better, if pruned. INTEGRATE, as a short block beside rem:handicap-base/prop:hz: ht:def-visits, ht:lem-sigmin, ht:lem-nonstat, ht:lem-sigma (the two lemmas in the LaTeX are the actual mathematical content and should be kept as lemmas), ht:thm-kappa, ht:cor-rlambda, ht:rem-freeze -- with three sentences the route did not write: that kappa and the claim are round 13's (v11), now proved with constants; that rem:lcp's attributed prior art already gives all of R by interior-point methods, so this is the import-free version inside the four-import rule; and that prop:hz's paragraph is its special case (prop:hz should then cite it rather than argue by row masses). INTEGRATE COMPRESSED, as one or two sentences inside rem:handicap-base rather than a proposition: ht:prop-damping (games built and verified, but the witness has P_0 = P_1). DO NOT INTEGRATE: ht:prop-cutform (restatement), ht:prop-tworounds (already recorded for BC(2,s)), ht:cor-cutwidth's Phi recursion (never a contraction; at most keep the one-cut inequality max_{P'} u_{v,ibar} <= q(x)/M(v,i) as a clause), and none of next_steps item 1.
